Subject: Data residency & end-of-contract erase: BetaHealth private VPC

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the earlier demo. As BetaHealth works through the security review, we need to confirm Redwood's exact process for finalizing a private/VPC deployment when we offboard. Specifically we need:

- A short, step-by-step runbook that shows how customer-controlled object/storage artifacts are deleted (including snapshots, versioned buckets, and cross-region replicas).
- How KMS key destruction is handled (do you destroy customer-managed keys or rotate/revoke?).
- Whether there is any residual metadata retained in the Redwood control plane and for how long.
- An evidentiary artifact we can present to our auditors showing the delete occurred (signed manifest, checksums, timestamps).

Can you also confirm typical timelines (we're trying to set expectations in our contract): how long from request until final attestation? We prefer SHA256 manifests for deleted object lists if possible.

Elena Morales
Head of Security Operations
BetaHealth

P.S. We may need SOC2 evidence correlated to the wipe dates — please call out what you can provide without a separate audit engagement.

Subject: Re: Data residency & end-of-contract erase: BetaHealth private VPC

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I've looped in Karthik (infra) and Marissa (trust) and attached our working runbook and a short residency checklist. High level plan below — happy to go over on a quick call.

Proposed two-phase workflow (customer-controlled storage in private VPC):
1) Pre-wipe validation (3 business days): freeze writes, confirm snapshot inventory, export object manifest.
2) Scheduled purge (1–7 business days depending on volume): delete versioned objects, delete snapshots, remove cross-region replicas, purge tombstones where applicable.
3) KMS action (same-day as purge or scheduled): revoke keys used to encrypt customer data; optional key-destruction where customer requests cryptographic sanitization.
4) Evidence generation (up to 10 business days): signed manifest (SHA256 list), storage provider deletion logs, and a Redwood attestation PDF with timestamps and operator IDs.

Deliverables we can provide without extra audit work: signed manifest, deletion logs, attestation letter referencing runbook steps. For SOC2 artifacts that tie to internal controls, we can correlate timestamps to SOC2 control IDs in our report; formal SOC2 + project-specific evidence may require 1–2 weeks to compile.

Next steps: please confirm whether BetaHealth requires cryptographic key destruction (vs. key revocation) and whether an on-call witness from your side will want to join the purge. If you confirm, we'll schedule a 30-minute technical call and lock a purge window.

Attachments: VPC_Erase_Runbook_v1.pdf, Data-Residency-Checklist.xlsx

—
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena — quick technical notes to augment Tessa's plan. I'll list practical behaviors we follow in our Private/VPC packaging: 

- Object storage: if bucket versioning was enabled, we delete all versions and then the object markers; for providers with eventual consistency we wait for confirmation events and then compile the deletion manifest. We capture SHA256 for objects we can access and include the manifest as part of the attestation.
- Snapshots & images: block volume snapshots are deleted in the cloud tenant; we then verify absence via API and include the snapshot delete response IDs in the manifest.
- Cross-region replication: replication rules are removed before deletion; replicated copies are located and deleted as part of the purge.
- KMS: we support both revocation (quick) and key material destruction (longer; irreversible). If you request destruction, we'll schedule it for the end of the purge window and return a signed KMS destruction receipt.
- Control plane metadata: by default, control plane operational metadata (job IDs, request logs) is retained for 90 days to support post-wipe troubleshooting. For customers that require reduced retention we can shrink this to 30 days contractually or extract and delete project-specific metadata as an add-on.

Evidence we can produce: deletion manifest (SHA256 where available), cloud deletion API receipts, operator-signed attestation PDF, and an optional notarized attestation via DocuSign. If BetaHealth needs cryptographic hashes for every deleted object but objects are encrypted with customer-managed keys, we'll need access to unencrypted digests or to compute them prior to encryption — let's confirm that on the call.

Elena — adding trust & compliance context. A few committed SLAs and outputs we can promise in our standard Private agreement: 

- Primary erase window: target completion within 30 calendar days after formal offboard request for typical-sized deployments (small to medium). Large archives may require extended windows; we'll provide schedule during the pre-wipe validation.
- Attestation delivery: Redwood will provide a signed attestation package within 10 business days after the final purge, including the deletion manifest and cloud receipts.
- Control plane metadata retention: default 90 days; contractually reducible to 30 days with a data handback addendum.
- SOC2 correlation: we can map purge activities to SOC2 control objectives and include the mapping in the attestation. If BetaHealth requires an SOC2 auditor letter tied directly to the purge event, that is treated as a supplementary engagement.

Attachments: Erase-Attestation-Template.docx

If these timelines work, I'll prepare the attestation template for your security team to review prior to the purge. Also: DocuSign option is available for signatures and notarized attestation.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks — this is helpful and close to what we need. A few clarifying items before we lock the purge window: 

1) We do want cryptographic key destruction for the key material used to encrypt customer blobs (irreversible) — please include the signed KMS destruction receipt in the attestation.
2) For the SHA256 manifest: we can compute hashes on our side prior to encryption if Redwood can accept a pre-shared manifest to match against deletion receipts. Is there a secure channel/process you recommend for transferring that pre-wipe manifest?
3) Proposed times for a 30-minute call next week (all times PST): Wed 05/26 10–11am, Thu 05/27 2–3pm. Security Ops (Tom) will join.

If you can confirm the secure transfer mechanism and that KMS destruction receipts will be part of the attestation, we can go ahead and schedule.
